subject: Linewright

verdict.headline: Good, not yet great. The core is eroding quietly while the founder considers a new product.
verdict.hedgehog: Linewright makes every professional subtitle file pass the client's delivery spec the first time. The studio sets the rules once, every freelancer's editor enforces them, and the business earns from seats that renew.
verdict.weakest_link: Profit isn't turning into spec-checker progress. Your hours go to licensing tickets and bug-fix releases.
verdict.brutal_fact: Renewals fell four quarters in a row (64% → 52%), below your 58% model. Lantern's free auto-align is the reason 69% of buyers chose you, and it ships stable this winter.
missing_numbers: The renewal rate split into studios vs. individuals

confidence.rests_on: The facts are solid. The Hedgehog rests on studio calls and one survey.

takeaways.hedgehog: Be the tool that makes subtitle files pass spec the first time
takeaways.people: Hire part-time support first, then a release backup

great_version: The reference tool for spec-compliant subtitles. A studio loads a broadcaster's delivery rules once, and every freelancer's file then passes QC on the first try, with a per-file report to prove it. Studio seats are most of the revenue and almost never churn. It runs on a small, calm team and stays narrow: not a creator app, not a Linux project, not a workflow platform.

hedgehog.sentence: Linewright makes every professional subtitle file pass the client's delivery spec the first time, with rules set once by the studio and enforced in every freelancer's editor, and earns its living from seats that renew.

weakest.why: The surplus exists (about $60k retained, $88k in the bank), but it isn't buying spec-engine progress. Your 50 hours go to about 30 install and licensing tickets a week, and the last two releases were bug fixes.

current_push: Free your hours: remove the root causes of licensing and install tickets and add part-time support.

flywheel.doom_loop: Not in one, but close. Four options you keep circling, a six-month pivot into a different market, and a Linux port started because of forum requests. A creator pivot right after Lantern's release would be the classic doom-loop move.

stop_doing.why: A different product, buyer and platform, and six months of the only engineer's time during the core's riskiest six months. The waitlist came from one borrowed post, and the "50x market" figure is unverified.
46 forum requests is not a business case unless a paying studio needs it.
Keep it at parity and stop making it the headline.

faith_statement: Professional subtitles always have to pass someone's spec, and no free editor or workflow platform owns that problem the way a tool built by a subtitler can.
truth_climate: Your notes record the bad numbers honestly, then explain them away. Add a quarterly one-page scorecard with split renewal rates and a cancellation-reason prompt.
